To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hypoxia and anemic conditions, which are frequently found in locally advanced solid tumors (e.g., head and neck, cervix uteri, breast, lung, and bladder cancer), are associated with an increased risk of local tumor recurrence, distant metastases, and death, and that the mechanisms of tumor progression and treatment resistance induced by these conditions are not identical but rather complementary.
tumor hypoxia is a major determinant of tumor progression and treatment resistance.

(i) tumor hypoxia and anemic tumor-associated anemia are common in patients with advanced solid tumors; (ii) hypoxia and tumor-associated anemia may contribute to tumor progression, and may compromise the efficacy of radio- and chemotherapy; (iii) tumor hypoxemia and tumor-associated anemic hypoxia may be overcome or attenuated by the administration of recombinant human Erythropoietin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How does anemia and hypoxia influence tumor biology and treatment outcome?

the following issues: (1) The impact of hypoxia on the biology and treatment response of locally advanced solid tumor cells; (2) The impact of anemia on the biology and response to treatment of locally advanced solid cancer cells; (3) The impact of tumor hypoxemia on the tumor response to treatment; (4) The impact of treatment on the tumor response and the tumor microvasular network.

(1) the elucidation of the molecular and cellular basis of hypoxia and anemic-induced treatment resistance; (2) the identification of hypoxia- and/or anemia-induced molecular targets that are involved in the acquisition of resistance; and (3) the development of strategies for the reversal of hypoxic- and/or anemic-induced treatment failure and the improvement of treatment outcome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoxia and anemic conditions are both associated with an unfavorable prognosis, and that the presence of both hypoxia and tumor-associated anemia may further aggravate the situation.

hypoxia and anemic conditions may contribute to the development and maintenance of a more aggressive phenotype, which may be associated with a more malignant phenotype, and may be associated with an increased risk of local and systemic failure.
hypoxia/anemia is not only an important factor contributing to tumor progression but also a major obstacle to successful tumor control by radiation or chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia and anemic conditions may be considered as two major factors that can influence tumor biology and response to therapy.
hypoxia is a key determinant of tumor progression and treatment resistance.
hypoxia is a major factor contributing to treatment resistance, and that tumor-associated anemia may further aggravate the hypoxic situation in locally advanced solid tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxia and/or anemia can have major implications for the biology of the tumor, its response to treatment and ultimately the survival of the patient.
hypoxia and anemic conditions should be considered as a major determinant of treatment outcome in patients with locally advanced solid tumors.
hypoxia and anemic conditions are not only a consequence of tumor growth, but that they are actively contributing to tumor progression.
